newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Aeroflot allowed to pick up passengers at Shannon.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot allowed to pick up passengers at Shannon.

text.p: Aeroflot, the Russian state airline, was given the green light to pick up local passenger traffic between Shannon and New York, Irish minister for Transport, Energy and Communications, Alan Dukes said on Monday.

Dukes made his announcement during a ground-breaking ceremony at Ireland's western airport, Shannon, to mark a new 23.5 million Irish pound expansion to passenger terminal facilities, which he said would create 200 construction jobs.
Aeroflot hopes to begin selling seats on the route in September, Dukes said in a statement.
The new rights - known as fifth freedom rights - allow Aeroflot to sell 60 passenger seats per flight on three services a week in summer and two weekly winter services.
The Russian airline already has such rights for flights to all points in Central and South America and for Washington and Miami.
